name: Hamas
summary: Palestinian Islamist political and armed movement. It took control of Gaza in 2007 and led the 7 October 2023 attacks against Israel.
economy: Funding has included external support, donations and revenues collected under its Gaza administration.
military: Political organization with an armed wing, the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades.
origin: Founded in Gaza during the first intifada, emerging from the Palestinian Muslim Brotherhood.
decline: Severe leadership and military losses during the war beginning in 2023; the organization persisted as of the source date.
recognition: A non-state movement, distinct from the State of Palestine. Designated a terrorist organization by the United States and several other governments.

sources.title: CFR: What Is Hamas?
CRS: Hamas: Background, Current Status, and U.S. Policy

name: Houthis / Ansar Allah
summary: Yemeni political and armed movement rooted in Zaydi revivalism. It seized Sana’a in 2014 and remains a principal party to Yemen’s unresolved war.
capital: No sovereign capital; Sana’a is the principal seat of its de facto administration.
military: Armed movement with de facto governing institutions; receives support from Iran.
origin: Grew from a northern Yemeni Zaydi movement into an insurgency against the central government.
recognition: Distinct from Yemen’s internationally recognized government. The United States redesignated it a Foreign Terrorist Organization in March 2025.

name: Al-Qaeda
summary: Transnational jihadist terrorist network established by Osama bin Laden, responsible for the 11 September 2001 attacks and sustained through regional affiliates.
military: Decentralized terrorist network with regional affiliates.
origin: Formed from foreign veterans and support networks of the anti-Soviet war in Afghanistan.
decline: Central leadership weakened by counterterrorism campaigns; affiliates remained active in the UN’s February 2026 assessment.
recognition: Subject to the UN ISIL and Al-Qaida sanctions regime; not a state.

name: Islamic State / ISIS
summary: Jihadist terrorist organization originating in al-Qaeda in Iraq. Its self-declared caliphate lost its final territorial stronghold in 2019; insurgent networks and affiliates persisted.
capital: No sovereign capital; Raqqa served as a de facto administrative centre during its territorial rule.
military: Insurgent and terrorist organization with regional affiliates.
origin: Developed from Zarqawi’s Iraq-based organization amid war in Iraq, later expanding during Syria’s civil war.
decline: Coalition and local forces dismantled its territorial rule in Iraq and Syria by 2019; the organization continued afterward.
recognition: Its caliphate claim had no sovereign recognition. Subject to the UN ISIL and Al-Qaida sanctions regime.

startBasis: 2004 marks al-Qaeda in Iraq; the ISIS name dates to 2013 and the caliphate claim to 2014.
sourceCutoff: The UN report considered information received through 2025-12-15.

name: Hezbollah
summary: Lebanese Shia political and armed organization backed by Iran. It combines participation in national politics with armed structures outside the Lebanese state.
rulers: Naim Qassem, secretary-general from October 2024; verified in the April 2026 source.
economy: Iranian financial support and associated organizational fundraising; no sovereign national economy.
military: Party-linked armed organization with separate political, military and social-service structures.
origin: Formed during Lebanon’s civil war and the 1982 Israeli invasion, with Iranian support.
decline: Israeli operations severely weakened its leadership in 2024; it remained active in the renewed conflict described in April 2026.
recognition: Designated a terrorist organization by the United States and several other governments; designation scope differs among jurisdictions.

sources.title: CFR: What Is Hezbollah?

name: Al-Shabaab
summary: Somali Islamist insurgent and terrorist organization that emerged from the Islamic Courts movement and formally joined al-Qaeda in 2012.
origin: Emerged from Somalia’s Islamic Courts movement during the conflict surrounding the courts’ rise and defeat.
decline: Continued insurgency and cross-border violence were documented in the February 2026 UN report.
recognition: UN-sanctioned non-state organization; designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization by the United States in 2008.

name: Rapid Support Forces
summary: Sudanese paramilitary force led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo. Its war with the Sudanese Armed Forces began in April 2023 and has caused widespread civilian devastation.
capital: No sovereign capital; its parallel government was reported based in Nyala in 2025–2026.
rulers: Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti), commander; verified in the September 2026 source.
economy: Gold-linked businesses and external financial networks have supported the force.
military: Paramilitary organization and allied armed groups.
origin: Established in 2013 from Janjaweed-linked forces used in Sudanese counterinsurgency campaigns.
recognition: A non-state belligerent in Sudan; its separate administration does not establish an internationally recognized new state.

name: Taiwan / Republic of China
summary: Self-governing democracy administered by the Republic of China. The People’s Republic of China claims Taiwan, while the two governments maintain separate political and military institutions.
rulers: Lai Ching-te, elected president in January 2024; verified by CRS in August 2025.
economy: Export-oriented economy with a major role in semiconductor and technology supply chains.
military: Separate armed forces under ROC civilian authorities.
contributions: Semiconductor manufacturing and global electronics supply chains.
origin: The ROC government relocated to Taiwan after its defeat on mainland China in 1949; political liberalization followed in the late twentieth century.
recognition: Limited formal diplomatic recognition alongside extensive unofficial relations. The PRC claim and Taiwan’s self-government must be represented separately.

name: State of Palestine
summary: State proclaimed in 1988 and a UN non-member observer state since 2012. Recognition, occupation and the extent of effective Palestinian administration are separate questions.
capital: Jerusalem is the declared capital; sovereignty and administration are disputed.
currency: Israeli new shekel, Jordanian dinar and US dollar; no national currency is issued.
economy: War has devastated Gaza’s economy and infrastructure; movement restrictions and fiscal pressures also constrain economic activity in the West Bank.
origin: Proclaimed by the Palestine National Council on 15 November 1988 as an expression of Palestinian self-determination.
decline: Ongoing statehood and territorial dispute as of 2026-09-24.
recognition: UN non-member observer state, recognized by many countries; not a UN member state. This record is separate from Hamas.

name: Kosovo
summary: Republic that declared independence from Serbia in 2008. It is recognized by many states, while Serbia and several other governments dispute its sovereignty.
currency: Euro; unilateral use does not make Kosovo a euro-area member.
economy: Growth relies partly on domestic demand, remittances and investment. The IMF estimated 3.6% real GDP growth for 2025 in April 2026.
military: Kosovo Security Force; NATO-led KFOR has a separate international security mandate.
origin: Independence followed the 1998–1999 war and a period of UN administration.
recognition: Partially recognized state; EU institutions use a status-neutral designation. Recognition and territorial administration must not be conflated.

name: Somaliland
summary: Self-governing polity that declared independence from Somalia in 1991. Israel recognized it in December 2025; Somalia rejects its secession.
currency: Somaliland shilling; US dollars also circulate.
economy: Livestock exports, remittances, services and trade through Berbera are significant.
origin: Declared renewed independence in 1991 during the collapse of Somalia’s central government.
recognition: Israel announced recognition on 26 December 2025. The UN Security Council continues to affirm Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

name: Northern Cyprus
summary: Self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, administering the island’s north. Only Türkiye recognizes it as an independent state; the Cyprus settlement remains unresolved.
capital: North Nicosia / Lefkoşa (seat of the de facto administration).
currency: Turkish lira; other currencies are also used.
economy: Tourism, agriculture, services and cross-community trade; closely linked to Türkiye’s financial system.
military: Local security forces alongside a Turkish military presence.
origin: Proclaimed in 1983 after the island’s division following the 1974 conflict.
recognition: Recognized only by Türkiye. The Republic of Cyprus is internationally recognized over the island, subject to the UK sovereign base areas.

name: Abkhazia
summary: Breakaway polity on Georgia’s Black Sea coast, supported by Russia. Georgia and most states regard the territory as part of Georgia.
military: De facto security structures with a Russian military presence.
origin: The 1992–1993 war separated the territory from Georgian central government control.
recognition: Recognized by Russia and a small number of other states; the EU supports Georgia’s internationally recognized borders.

name: South Ossetia / Tskhinvali region
summary: Breakaway polity within Georgia’s internationally recognized borders. Its de facto institutions and security remain closely tied to Russia.
currency: Russian ruble (documented in the 2010 institutional study; a current currency review is pending).
economy: Historically highly dependent on Russian financial assistance; current economic measures are not verified here.
military: De facto security structures and Russian forces; no current deployment map is supplied.
origin: Armed conflict during the Soviet collapse led to a 1992 ceasefire; the 2008 war deepened separation from Georgia.
recognition: Recognized by Russia and a small number of other states. The EU rejects the legality of its separate presidential elections.

name: Transnistria / Transdniestria
summary: Self-proclaimed polity centred on Tiraspol, internationally regarded as part of Moldova. De facto separation persisted after the 1992 war.
currency: Transnistrian ruble (introduced in 1994; current monetary details require a newer source).
economy: Industrial and trading economy with strong energy dependence; a severe energy shock in 2025 exposed the fragility of its economic model.
origin: Local leaders proclaimed a separate republic in September 1990 amid disputes over language, sovereignty and the Soviet collapse.
recognition: Not recognized by UN member states. International settlement efforts seek a solution within Moldova’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

name: Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic / Western Sahara
summary: SADR claims independence for Western Sahara. Morocco administers most of the territory and claims sovereignty; the UN treats Western Sahara as a non-self-governing territory.
capital: Laayoune / El Aaiún is claimed; the SADR administration operates in exile in Algeria.
military: Polisario Front armed forces; territorial claims are distinct from effective control.
origin: The Polisario Front proclaimed the SADR in 1976 as Spain withdrew from Western Sahara.
decline: Ongoing dispute as of 2025-06-12; the 1991 ceasefire broke down in 2020.
recognition: SADR is an African Union member recognized by some states. Western Sahara’s final status remains unresolved in the UN process.
